description: Let your agents buy anything. SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Rust), CLI, OpenAPI spec and agent plugins for OpenIntents.

files.content:
# Examples

Each example sends the same intent, waits, and prints the receipt or the
payment link. Set `OPENINTENTS_API_KEY` to a test key (`oi_test_...`) first:
test intents run end to end but never charge.

| Language | File | Run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TypeScript | [`buy-coffee.ts`](buy-coffee.ts) | `npx tsx sdk/examples/buy-coffee.ts` |
| Python | [`buy_coffee.py`](buy_coffee.py) | `uv run --with openintents sdk/examples/buy_coffee.py` |
| Rust | [`../rust/examples/buy_coffee.rs`](../rust/examples/buy_coffee.rs) | `cd sdk/rust && cargo run --example buy_coffee` |

# SDKs

| Path | Package | Registry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`typescript/`](typescript) | `@tinyhumansai/openintents` (SDK + `openintents` CLI) | npm |
| [`python/`](python) | `openintents` (sync + async) | PyPI |
| [`rust/`](rust) | `openintents` (async; CLI behind `--features cli`) | crates.io |
| [`skill/openintents/`](skill/openintents) | Agent skill (`SKILL.md`) | |
| [`plugin-claude/`](plugin-claude) | Claude Code plugin (MCP server + skill) | this repo's marketplace |
| [`examples/`](examples) | One runnable example per language | |

All three SDKs implement the same surface, generated by hand from
[`../spec/openapi.yaml`](../spec/openapi.yaml). Every create (intents,
customers, top-ups, sessions), `cancel`, an answer to an input request,
session `release` and session command sends an `Idempotency-Key`, so a
retry never runs anything twice;
making a profile is idempotent by itself. Intents can be bought for, and
listed by, a `customer`. Event streams follow a timeline over Server-Sent
Events: they resume after a dropped connection with `Last-Event-ID`, and end
when the API answers `204` (the timeline is over).

| Operation | TypeScript | Python | Rust |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create | `intents.create` | `intents.create` | `create_intent` |
| Retrieve | `intents.get` | `intents.get` | `get_intent` |
| List / all pages | `intents.list` / `listAll` | `intents.list` / `list_all` | `list_intents` |
| Cancel | `intents.cancel` | `intents.cancel` | `cancel_intent` |
| Answer an input request | `intents.input` | `intents.input` | `answer_intent_input` |
| Wait | `intents.wait` | `intents.wait` | `wait` |
| Intent events: page / live stream | `intents.listEvents` / `streamEvents` | `intents.list_events` / `stream_events` | `list_intent_events` / `stream_intent_events` |
| Balance (a customer's) | `balance.get({ customer })` | `balance.get(customer=)` | `balance` / `balance_for` |
| Customers: create, retrieve, update | `customers.create` / `get` / `update` | `customers.create` / `get` / `update` | `create_customer` / `get_customer` / `update_customer` |
| Customers: list / all pages | `customers.list` / `listAll` | `customers.list` / `list_all` | `list_customers` |
| Top-ups: create, retrieve | `topups.create` / `get` | `topups.create` / `get` | `create_topup` / `get_topup` |
| Profiles: create, retrieve, forget | `profiles.create` / `get` / `forget` | `profiles.create` / `get` / `forget` | `create_profile` / `get_profile` / `forget_profile` |
| Profiles: list / all pages | `profiles.list` / `listAll` | `profiles.list` / `list_all` | `list_profiles` |
| Sessions: open, retrieve, release | `sessions.create` / `get` / `release` | `sessions.create` / `get` / `release` | `create_session` / `get_session` / `release_session` |
| Sessions: list / all pages | `sessions.list` / `listAll` | `sessions.list` / `list_all` | `list_sessions` |
| Session commands: run, retrieve | `sessions.runCommand` / `getCommand` | `sessions.run_command` / `get_command` | `run_session_command` / `get_session_command` |
| Session screenshot (JPEG bytes) | `sessions.screenshot` | `sessions.screenshot` | `session_screenshot` |
| Session events: page / live stream | `sessions.listEvents` / `streamEvents` | `sessions.list_events` / `stream_events` | `list_session_events` / `stream_session_events` |
| Errors | `OpenIntentsError` | `OpenIntentsError` | `Error::Api` |
| Webhooks (intent and session events) | `verifyWebhook` | `verify_webhook` | `webhooks::verify_webhook` |

Errors carry the API's `status`, `type` (`kind` in Rust), `code`, `param` and,
with `profile_busy`, the `lease` that says what holds the profile.

`wait` returns when the intent is final, or waits on a person: payment
(`requires_payment`, `returnOnPayment` / `return_on_payment`), an answer
from the payer while the agent signs them in to the shop or for a `detail`
the purchase needs (`requires_input`, `returnOnInput` / `return_on_input`;
a detail's choices are in `input_request.options`), or the payer's sign-in
to the shop (`requires_login`, `returnOnSignIn` / `return_on_sign_in`). All
three are on by default.

Versions move together; `node sdk/bump-versions.mjs <patch|minor|major>` bumps
all of them.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  typescript:
    name: TypeScript
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents lint
      - run: pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents test
      - run: pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents build

  python:
    name: Python ${{ matrix.python }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python: ["3.10", "3.13"]
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: sdk/python
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - run: uv run --extra dev ruff check src tests
      - run: uv run --extra dev ruff format --check src tests
      - run: uv run --extra dev pytest

  rust:
    name: Rust
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: sdk/rust
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: sdk/rust
      - run: cargo fmt --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets --features cli -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo test --locked

"""uv run --with openintents sdk/examples/buy_coffee.py  (needs OPENINTENTS_API_KEY; use an oi_test_ key)"""

from openintents import OpenIntents

with OpenIntents() as oi:
    created = oi.intents.create("flat white, oat milk, pickup 8:45 at the Blue Bottle on 5th", max_amount=1000)
    print("created", created["id"])

    intent = oi.intents.wait(created["id"])
    if intent["status"] == "requires_payment":
        print("Pay here:", intent["payment"]["payment_url"])
    elif intent["status"] == "completed":
        print("Receipt:", intent["result"])
    else:
        print(f"Ended as {intent['status']}:", (intent.get("error") or {}).get("message"))

# OpenIntents plugin for Claude Code

Adds the hosted OpenIntents MCP server and the `openintents` skill to Claude
Code, so you can ask for purchases in plain language ("get me a flat white
from the Blue Bottle on 5th, pickup 8:45, max $10").

```text
/plugin marketplace add tinyhumansai/openintents
/plugin install openintents@openintents
```

The server takes an API key: make one at
<https://openintents.io/dashboard/api-keys> (start with a test key,
`oi_test_...`: test intents run end to end but never charge) and set it as
`OPENINTENTS_API_KEY` before starting Claude Code. The plugin's server sends
it as `Authorization: Bearer`. Prefer a one-off server without the plugin?

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http openintents https://api.openintents.io/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $OPENINTENTS_API_KEY"
```

See <https://openintents.io/docs/mcp>.

# openintents (Python)

Python SDK for [OpenIntents](https://openintents.io), the agentic API to buy
anything. Send an intent in plain language; the API does the agentic work in a
real browser, gets it paid, and resolves to a receipt. Inference, browser,
compute and bandwidth are free.

> Preview: the API is still being built, so it may change before launch.

```bash
pip install openintents
```

## Usage

```python
from openintents import OpenIntents

oi = OpenIntents()  # reads OPENINTENTS_API_KEY

intent = oi.intents.create(
    "flat white, oat milk, pickup 8:45 at the Blue Bottle on 5th",
    max_amount=1000,  # cents: never spend more than $10.00
)

intent = oi.intents.wait(intent["id"])  # returns when final, or when it needs payment

if intent["status"] == "requires_payment":
    print("Pay here:", intent["payment"]["payment_url"])
elif intent["status"] == "completed":
    receipt = intent["result"]
    print(receipt["merchant"], receipt["total"], receipt["confirmation"])
```

Async:

```python
from openintents import AsyncOpenIntents

async with AsyncOpenIntents() as oi:
    intent = await oi.intents.create("book an Uber to SFO at 7am", max_amount=6000)
    intent = await oi.intents.wait(intent["id"])
```

Also: `oi.intents.get(id)`, `oi.intents.list(status=..., customer=..., limit=...)`,
`oi.intents.list_all()`, `oi.intents.cancel(id)`, `oi.balance.get(customer=...)`,
`oi.customers.create/get/update/list/list_all` and `oi.topups.create/get`.
Pass `customer=` to `intents.create` to buy for one of your customers.
Errors raise `OpenIntentsError` (`status`, `type`, `code`, `param`, and
`lease` with `profile_busy`); 429s, 5xx and network errors are retried with
backoff. Every create (but a profile's), `cancel`, `release` and
`run_command` sends an `Idempotency-Key` automatically.

## Live events

Follow an intent as it runs. The stream resumes by itself after a dropped
connection, and ends once the intent is over:

```python
for event in oi.intents.stream_events(intent["id"]):
    print(event["type"], event["data"])  # status, step, checkout
```

`oi.intents.list_events(id, limit=..., cursor=...)` pages the same timeline.
On `AsyncOpenIntents`, `stream_events` is an async iterator: `async for`.

## Browser sessions

A session opens a payer's browser profile without an intent: to sign them in
to a shop once, so later intents find them signed in. A session never pays
or places an order.

```python
session = oi.sessions.create(customer="cus_4b81d0", start_url="https://shop.example/login")
for event in oi.sessions.stream_events(session["id"]):
    if event["type"] == "status" and event["data"]["status"] == "open":
        break
page = oi.sessions.run_command(session["id"], {"type": "snapshot"})  # page["snapshot"] has the refs
oi.sessions.run_command(session["id"], {"type": "act", "ref": "e12", "action": "type", "text": "ada@example.com"})
jpeg = oi.sessions.screenshot(session["id"])  # bytes
oi.sessions.release(session["id"])  # the profile keeps the sign-in
```

Also `oi.sessions.list/list_all/get/get_command/list_events` and
`oi.profiles.list/list_all/create/get/forget`.

## Webhooks

```python
from openintents import verify_webhook, WebhookVerificationError

event = verify_webhook(request_body_bytes, request.headers.get("OpenIntents-Signature"), "whsec_...")
```

Session events (`session.opened`, `session.closed`, `session.failed`) carry a
session in `data`: check `event["type"]` first.

## Development

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest
uv run --extra dev ruff check src tests
```

Docs: <https://openintents.io/docs>. License: GPL-3.0-or-later.

# @tinyhumansai/openintents

TypeScript SDK and CLI for [OpenIntents](https://openintents.io), the agentic
API to buy anything. Send an intent in plain language; the API does the
agentic work in a real browser, gets it paid, and resolves to a receipt.
Inference, browser, compute and bandwidth are free.

> Preview: the API is still being built, so it may change before launch.

```bash
npm install @tinyhumansai/openintents
```

Zero runtime dependencies. Works in Node 20.3+, Bun, Deno and edge runtimes
(uses `fetch` and Web Crypto).

## SDK

```ts
import { OpenIntents } from "@tinyhumansai/openintents";

const oi = new OpenIntents(); // reads OPENINTENTS_API_KEY

const created = await oi.intents.create({
  intent: "flat white, oat milk, pickup 8:45 at the Blue Bottle on 5th",
  max_amount: 1000, // cents: never spend more than $10.00
});

const intent = await oi.intents.wait(created.id); // final, or needs payment

if (intent.status === "requires_payment") {
  console.log("Pay here:", intent.payment?.payment_url);
} else if (intent.status === "completed") {
  console.log(intent.result?.merchant, intent.result?.total);
}
```

Also: `oi.intents.get(id)`, `oi.intents.list({ status, customer, limit })`,
`for await (const i of oi.intents.listAll())`, `oi.intents.cancel(id)`,
`oi.intents.input(id, { input, value })` (see below),
`oi.balance.get({ customer })`, `oi.customers.create/get/update/list/listAll`
and `oi.topups.create/get`. Pass `customer` to `intents.create` to buy for one
of your customers. Errors throw `OpenIntentsError` (`status`, `type`, `code`,
`param`, and `lease` with `profile_busy`). Every create (but a profile's),
`cancel`, `input`, `release` and `runCommand` sends an `Idempotency-Key`
automatically; 429s, 5xx and network errors are retried with backoff.

### Signing in to a shop

When a shop wants the payer signed in and asks for a phone number or email
and then a code, the agent signs them in itself. Each time it needs
something only the payer knows, `wait` returns the intent in
`requires_input`. Ask the payer `input_request.prompt` and answer within 5
minutes; the agent's model never sees the answer:

```ts
if (intent.status === "requires_input" && intent.input_request) {
  const answer = await askThePayer(intent.input_request.prompt); // your chat, say
  await oi.intents.input(intent.id, { input: intent.input_request.id, value: answer });
  // or { input, decline: true }, or { input, done: true } for an approval
}
```

Or send the payer `input_request.url` to type it there themselves. Pass
`sign_in_hint: { phone }` or `{ email }` to `create` to skip the first
question. Passwords are never asked this way: those shops send a sign-in
link instead (`requires_login`, `sign_in.url`).

The same status asks for anything else the purchase needs that the request
did not give, such as the email the shop wants for the order or a size:
`input_request.kind` is then `detail`, `prompt` is the agent's own question,
and `options` lists the choices when there are any (answer with one of
them). Answer it the same way, with `value`; the answer goes back to the
agent. An intent asks at most 3 details, and never for a secret.

### Live events

Follow an intent as it runs. The stream resumes by itself after a dropped
connection, and ends once the intent is over:

```ts
for await (const event of oi.intents.streamEvents(created.id)) {
  console.log(event.type, event.data); // status, step, checkout
}
```

`oi.intents.listEvents(id, { limit, cursor })` pages the same timeline.

### Browser sessions

A session opens a payer's browser profile without an intent: to sign them in
to a shop once, so later intents find them signed in. A session never pays
or places an order.

```ts
const session = await oi.sessions.create({ customer: "cus_4b81d0", start_url: "https://shop.example/login" });
for await (const event of oi.sessions.streamEvents(session.id)) {
  if (event.type === "status" && event.data.status === "open") break;
}
const page = await oi.sessions.runCommand(session.id, { type: "snapshot" }); // page.snapshot has the refs
await oi.sessions.runCommand(session.id, { type: "act", ref: "e12", action: "type", text: "ada@example.com" });
const jpeg = await oi.sessions.screenshot(session.id); // Uint8Array
await oi.sessions.release(session.id); // the profile keeps the sign-in
```

Also `oi.sessions.list/listAll/get/getCommand/listEvents` and
`oi.profiles.list/listAll/create/get/forget`.

### Webhooks

```ts
import { verifyWebhook } from "@tinyhumansai/openintents";

// Use the raw body, before JSON parsing.
const event = await verifyWebhook(rawBody, req.headers.get("OpenIntents-Signature"), process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET!);
if (event.type === "intent.requires_payment") notify(event.data.payment?.payment_url);
```

Session events (`session.opened`, `session.closed`, `session.failed`) carry
a session in `data`: check `event.type` first.

## CLI

```bash
npm install -g @tinyhumansai/openintents
openintents login
openintents run "UberX to SFO, leaving 7am" --max 60 --wait
openintents status <id> --wait --json
openintents pay <id>      # open the payment link
openintents input <id> --input <input id> --value <code>
openintents balance
```

Exit codes: `0` completed, `1` failed or error, `2` needs payment, `3`
cancelled, `4` needs the payer to sign in to the shop (`sign_in.url`), `5`
needs an answer from the payer (`input_request.prompt`).

## Development

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents lint
pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents test
pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents build
```

Docs: <https://openintents.io/docs>. License: GPL-3.0-or-later.

import json

import httpx
import pytest

from openintents import AsyncOpenIntents, OpenIntents, OpenIntentsError, WaitTimeoutError


def intent(**over):
    return {
        "id": "int_1",
        "object": "intent",
        "status": "queued",
        "intent": "flat white",
        "test": True,
        "created_at": "2026-10-01T08:30:00Z",
        **over,
    }


def transport(*responses, calls=None):
    queue = list(responses)

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        if calls is not None:
            calls.append(request)
        status, body = queue.pop(0) if len(queue) > 1 else queue[0]
        return httpx.Response(status, json=body)

    return handler


def client(*responses, calls=None, **kw):
    http = httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(transport(*responses, calls=calls)))
    return OpenIntents(
        "oi_test_x", base_url="https://api.test/v1", http_client=http, max_retries=kw.get("max_retries", 0)
    )


def test_requires_api_key(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("OPENINTENTS_API_KEY", raising=False)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="API key"):
        OpenIntents()


def test_create_sends_auth_body_and_idempotency_key():
    calls = []
    oi = client((201, intent()), calls=calls)
    got = oi.intents.create("flat white", max_amount=1000)
    assert got["id"] == "int_1"
    req = calls[0]
    assert str(req.url) == "https://api.test/v1/intents"
    assert req.headers["authorization"] == "Bearer oi_test_x"
    assert len(req.headers["idempotency-key"]) == 36
    assert json.loads(req.content) == {"intent": "flat white", "max_amount": 1000}


def test_list_query_and_list_all_pagination():
    calls = []
    oi = client(
        (200, {"object": "list", "data": [intent(id="a")], "next_cursor": "a"}),
        (200, {"object": "list", "data": [intent(id="b")], "next_cursor": None}),
        calls=calls,
    )
    assert [i["id"] for i in oi.intents.list_all(status="completed")] == ["a", "b"]
    assert calls[0].url.params["status"] == "completed"
    assert calls[1].url.params["cursor"] == "a"


def test_errors_are_typed():
    oi = client(
        (400, {"error": {"type": "invalid_request", "code": "max_amount_too_low", "message": "too low"}})
    )
    with pytest.raises(OpenIntentsError) as exc:
        oi.intents.create("x")
    assert exc.value.status == 400
    assert exc.value.code == "max_amount_too_low"


def test_retries_5xx():
    calls = []
    oi = client((503, {}), (200, intent()), calls=calls, max_retries=1)
    oi._max_retries = 1
    assert oi.intents.get("int_1")["id"] == "int_1"
    assert len(calls) == 2


def test_wait_returns_payment_link():
    payment = {
        "reason": "insufficient_balance",
        "payment_url": "https://pay/p",
        "total": 550,
        "fee": 28,
        "currency": "usd",
        "expires_at": "x",
    }
    oi = client((200, intent(status="running")), (200, intent(status="requires_payment", payment=payment)))
    got = oi.intents.wait("int_1", interval=0.001)
    assert got["payment"]["payment_url"] == "https://pay/p"


def test_wait_past_payment_and_timeout():
    oi = client((200, intent(status="requires_payment")), (200, intent(status="completed")))
    assert oi.intents.wait("int_1", interval=0.001, return_on_payment=False)["status"] == "completed"
    oi2 = client((200, intent(status="running")))
    with pytest.raises(WaitTimeoutError):
        oi2.intents.wait("int_1", interval=0.01, timeout=0.001)


def test_wait_returns_at_requires_login_with_the_link():
    sign_in = {"url": "https://openintents.io/signin/sgn_1", "shop": "amazon.com", "expires_at": "x"}
    oi = client((200, intent(status="running")), (200, intent(status="requires_login", sign_in=sign_in)))
    got = oi.intents.wait("int_1", interval=0)
    assert got["status"] == "requires_login"
    assert got["sign_in"]["url"] == "https://openintents.io/signin/sgn_1"


def test_create_sends_sign_in_link():
    calls = []
    oi = client((201, intent()), calls=calls)
    oi.intents.create("a lamp", sign_in_link=False)
    assert json.loads(calls[0].content) == {"intent": "a lamp", "sign_in_link": False}


def test_wait_keeps_polling_past_a_sign_in_when_asked():
    oi = client(
        (200, intent(status="requires_login")),
        (200, intent(status="queued")),
        (200, intent(status="completed")),
    )
    assert oi.intents.wait("int_1", interval=0, return_on_sign_in=False)["status"] == "completed"


INPUT_REQUEST = {
    "id": "inp_1",
    "kind": "code",
    "shop": "blinkit.com",
    "prompt": "Enter the code blinkit.com just sent to your phone.",
    "options": [],
    "channel": "sms",
    "length": 6,
    "url": "https://openintents.io/input/inp_1",
    "expires_at": "x",
    "attempts_left": 2,
}


def test_wait_returns_at_requires_input_with_what_to_ask():
    oi = client(
        (200, intent(status="running")),
        (200, intent(status="requires_input", input_request=INPUT_REQUEST)),
    )
    got = oi.intents.wait("int_1", interval=0)
    assert got["status"] == "requires_input"
    assert got["input_request"] == INPUT_REQUEST


def test_wait_returns_a_detail_with_its_options_answered_with_one():
    detail = {
        "id": "inp_2",
        "kind": "detail",
        "shop": "flipkart.com",
        "prompt": "Which size would you like?",
        "options": ["S", "M", "L"],
        "channel": None,
        "length": None,
        "url": "https://openintents.io/input/inp_2",
        "expires_at": "x",
        "attempts_left": 2,
    }
    calls = []
    oi = client(
        (200, intent(status="requires_input", input_request=detail)),
        (200, intent(status="running")),
        calls=calls,
    )
    request = oi.intents.wait("int_1", interval=0)["input_request"]
    assert request == detail
    assert request["kind"] == "detail" and request["options"] == ["S", "M", "L"]
    oi.intents.input("int_1", input=request["id"], value="M")
    assert json.loads(calls[1].content) == {"input": "inp_2", "value": "M"}


def test_wait_keeps_polling_past_an_input_request_when_asked():
    oi = client(
        (200, intent(status="requires_input")),
        (200, intent(status="running")),
        (200, intent(status="completed")),
    )

import pytest

from openintents import AsyncOpenIntents, OpenIntents, OpenIntentsError


def replay(*replies, calls=None):
    """A MockTransport handler: each request gets the next reply, and the last one repeats."""
    queue = list(replies)

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        if calls is not None:
            calls.append(request)
        reply = queue.pop(0) if len(queue) > 1 else queue[0]
        status, body = reply[0], reply[1]
        headers = reply[2] if len(reply) > 2 else None
        if isinstance(body, bytes):
            return httpx.Response(status, content=body, headers=headers)
        return httpx.Response(status, json=body, headers=headers)

    return handler


def client(*replies, calls=None):
    http = httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(replay(*replies, calls=calls)))
    return OpenIntents("oi_test_x", base_url="https://api.test/v1", http_client=http, max_retries=0)

# OpenIntents

OpenIntents is an agentic API for transactions: you send an intent in plain
language and it completes the purchase end to end, then returns a structured
receipt. Inference, browser, compute and bandwidth are free; completed
transactions carry a 5% fee that is shown on every receipt.

## Connect

Prefer the MCP tools (`create_intent`, `wait_for_intent`, `get_intent`,
`answer_input`, `list_intents`, `get_intent_events`, `cancel_intent`,
`get_balance`, `create_topup`, `get_topup`). The server takes the user's API
key (made at https://openintents.io/dashboard/api-keys), sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`. If the tools aren't available, with the key in
`OPENINTENTS_API_KEY`:

- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http openintents https://api.openintents.io/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $OPENINTENTS_API_KEY"`
- Codex: `codex mcp add openintents --url https://api.openintents.io/mcp --bearer-token-env-var OPENINTENTS_API_KEY`
- Otherwise use the CLI: `npm install -g @tinyhumansai/openintents`, then
  `openintents login` (or set `OPENINTENTS_API_KEY`).

## Send an intent

1. Turn the request into one specific sentence: what, where or from whom,
   when, and constraints ("flat white, oat milk, pickup 8:45 at the Blue Bottle
   on 5th").
2. Agree a budget with the user and always pass it as `max_amount` (cents), or
   `--max <dollars>` on the CLI.
3. Put structured details (addresses, names) in `context`, not the sentence.
   If the user has given you their phone number or email for signing in to
   the shop, you may pass it as `sign_in_hint` (`{ "phone": ... }` or
   `{ "email": ... }`) so the agent need not ask for it.
4. Create it and wait. Over MCP: `create_intent` with an `idempotency_key`
   of your choosing (send the same one if you retry, so it never buys twice),
   then `wait_for_intent`, again while the intent is still queued or running
   (each call waits up to 50 seconds). With the CLI:

   ```bash
   openintents run "flat white, oat milk, pickup 8:45 at the Blue Bottle on 5th" --max 10 --wait --json
   ```

5. Read the result:
   - `completed`: report merchant, items, total, fee and confirmation.
   - `requires_payment`: the balance can't cover it. Show the user what it is
     buying and give them `payment.payment_url`. Then wait again
     (`openintents status <id> --wait`).
   - `requires_input`: the agent is signing the user in to the shop
     (`input_request.shop`) and needs something only they know. Ask them
     exactly `input_request.prompt`, naming the shop. Send their reply right
     away, as the request expires in 5 minutes:
     `openintents input <id> --input <input_request.id> --value "<reply>"`,
     or `--done` once they approved an `approval`. If they would rather not,
     send `--decline`. Over MCP it is `answer_input` with the intent's `id`,
     `input` (`input_request.id`) and one of `value`, `done` or `decline`.
     If they would rather type it on a page than in the chat, give them
     `input_request.url` (theirs only). Then wait again. If
     the intent later shows `requires_login`, give them the sign-in link
     instead.

     When `input_request.kind` is `detail`, the purchase needs something the
     request did not give, such as the email the shop wants for the order,
     a size or a colour. Ask it the same way: exactly
     `input_request.prompt`, offering `input_request.options` as the choices
     when there are any. Send the user's reply with `--value` (one of the
     options, when there are any). The agent never asks for a secret this
     way: if a prompt ever asks for a password, a code, a PIN, card or bank
     details or an ID number, don't ask the user; send `--decline`.
   - `requires_login`: the shop wants the user signed in to their account
     there. Give the user `sign_in.url` (theirs only: it works on the first
     device that opens it), tell them it works for 30 minutes, and wait
     again once they say they're done.
   - `failed`: report `error.message`; ask before retrying.

CLI exit codes: 0 completed, 1 failed or error, 2 needs payment, 3 cancelled,
4 needs the user to sign in, 5 needs an answer from the user.

## Rules

- Only make purchases the user asked for, within the budget they gave.
- Never pay a payment link yourself, and never ask for, store or invent card
  numbers. Payment happens on the hosted payment page or from the balance.
- Never open a sign-in link or an `input_request.url` yourself. Never ask the
  user for a password, a card PIN, a UPI PIN or a bank OTP: ask only what
  `input_request.prompt` says, pass their reply on as it is, and don't
  store or repeat it.
- Use a test key (`oi_test_...`) when the user is only trying things out: test
  intents run end to end but never charge.
- Cancel (`openintents cancel <id>`) anything the user changes their mind
  about before it pays; cancelled intents are free.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, …) and contributors working in
this repository. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to this file: edit `AGENTS.md`.

> If a `CLAUDE.local.md` exists at the repo root, read it first. It holds
> personal, git-ignored notes that aren't part of this shared config.

## What this repo is

`tinyhumansai/openintents` is the **public, open-source** client side of
OpenIntents, the agentic API to buy anything: SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Rust),
the `openintents` CLI, the OpenAPI spec, an agent skill and a Claude Code
plugin. The hosted API, website and dashboard are **not** in this repo.

## This repository is public

Everything committed here is world-readable and permanent (forks and caches
keep it even after a revert). Before committing, make sure nothing private
comes along:

- **No secrets:** API keys (`oi_live_`/`oi_test_` values), webhook secrets
  (`whsec_`), tokens, `.env` files. Use obvious placeholders (`oi_test_...`).
- **No internal infrastructure:** hostnames other than the public
  `openintents.io` / `api.openintents.io`, cloud account or cluster details,
  deployment manifests, internal service names, dashboards or runbooks.
- **No references to private repositories or their paths**, internal tickets,
  customer data, or unreleased business details (pricing experiments,
  partners, roadmaps not already on the website).
- **Only public API behaviour:** describe what `spec/openapi.yaml` and the
  public docs say, not how the service implements it.

If a change would need private context to explain, it belongs somewhere else.

## Layout

| Path | Package | Toolchain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec/openapi.yaml` | | The v1 contract. Change it first, then the SDKs. |
| `sdk/typescript/` | `@tinyhumansai/openintents` (SDK + `openintents` bin) | Node 20.3+, pnpm 10, TypeScript, Vitest. Zero runtime deps. |
| `sdk/python/` | `openintents` | Python 3.10+, httpx, uv, pytest, ruff |
| `sdk/rust/` | `openintents` (CLI behind `--features cli`) | Rust stable, reqwest (rustls), wiremock |
| `sdk/skill/openintents/` | Agent skill; `SKILL.md` at the root links here | |
| `sdk/plugin-claude/` | Claude Code plugin; `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` lists it | |
| `sdk/examples/` | One runnable example per language | |

pnpm workspace (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`) covers `sdk/typescript` only.

## Commands (what CI runs)

```bash
# TypeScript
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents lint     # tsc --noEmit
pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents test     # vitest
pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents build

# Python (from sdk/python)
uv run --extra dev ruff check src tests
uv run --extra dev ruff format --check src tests
uv run --extra dev pytest

# Rust (from sdk/rust)
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --features cli -- -D warnings
cargo test
```

## Rules for SDK changes

- **Keep the three SDKs in parity.** Same operations, same defaults
  (`wait` returns on `requires_payment` unless told not to; 2 retries on
  429/5xx/network with backoff; automatic `Idempotency-Key` on create and
  cancel), same error fields. Update the parity table in `sdk/README.md`.
- **Spec first.** New fields or endpoints go in `spec/openapi.yaml`, then all
  SDKs, then the READMEs.
- **Be tolerant of new API data.** Unknown fields must not break parsing; Rust
  maps unknown statuses to `IntentStatus::Unknown`.
- **Webhook signatures are shared.** `OpenIntents-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`,
  HMAC-SHA256 of `"{t}.{raw body}"`, 300s tolerance, constant-time compare.
  Each suite asserts the same test vector; if you change signing, change all
  three.
- **Money is integer cents** everywhere; never floats in the API layer (the
  CLI's `--max` takes dollars and converts).
- **No new runtime dependencies** in the TypeScript SDK; keep Python to httpx.
- **Versions move together:** `node sdk/bump-versions.mjs <patch|minor|major>`.
  Don't hand-edit versions.
- **Tests with every change**, using mocked HTTP (Vitest mock fetch,
  `httpx.MockTransport`, wiremock). No test may call the real API.

## Style

- Plain, direct prose in docs and comments. **No em or en dashes** in any
  written copy; use a comma, colon or full stop.
- Comments explain why, not what. Public items get doc comments.
- Commit messages: conventional prefix (`feat(ts):`, `fix(python):`,
  `docs:`), small focused commits, no squashing of others' history.

## Releasing

Manual, via the **Release** workflow (`workflow_dispatch`): pick the SDKs and
the bump. It bumps all versions, commits to `main`, tags `vX.Y.Z` and
publishes the selected packages (npm with provenance, PyPI, crates.io).
Secrets: `NPM_TOKEN` and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (repository), and
`PYPI_API_TOKEN` on the `Production` environment (deployable from `main`
only).

# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please **do not open a public issue** for security problems. Report them
privately through GitHub's
[private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openintents/security/advisories/new)
for this repository.

Include what you found, how to reproduce it, and the impact you expect. We aim
to acknowledge reports within three business days and will keep you updated
until it's resolved. We're happy to credit you once a fix ships.

## Scope

This repository contains the client SDKs, CLI, spec and plugins. Issues in the
hosted API or website can be reported the same way.

## Handling keys

- Never commit API keys (`oi_live_...`, `oi_test_...`) or webhook secrets
  (`whsec_...`). If one leaks, revoke it in the dashboard immediately.
- The CLI stores a key saved with `openintents login` in
  `~/.config/openintents/config.json` with `0600` permissions.
- Always verify webhook signatures (`verifyWebhook` / `verify_webhook`) before
  trusting a payload.

name: Release

# Manual: tick the SDKs to publish and pick the bump. The prepare job bumps
# every SDK version together (sdk/bump-versions.mjs), commits to main and tags
# vX.Y.Z; each selected SDK is then published from that commit.
# Secrets: NPM_TOKEN, CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN (repository), PYPI_API_TOKEN (on the
# "Production" environment, which only main can deploy to).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      typescript:
        description: Publish the TypeScript SDK + CLI to npm
        type: boolean
        default: false
      python:
        description: Publish the Python SDK to PyPI
        type: boolean
        default: false
      rust:
        description: Publish the Rust SDK to crates.io
        type: boolean
        default: false
      bump:
        description: Version bump
        type: choice
        default: patch
        options: [patch, minor, major]

concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Bump, commit and tag
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    outputs:
      sha: ${{ steps.commit.outputs.sha }}
      version: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - name: Require at least one target
        if: ${{ !inputs.typescript && !inputs.python && !inputs.rust }}
        run: |
          echo "::error::Select at least one SDK to release."
          exit 1
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - id: bump
        run: echo "version=$(node sdk/bump-versions.mjs ${{ inputs.bump }})" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Refresh Cargo.lock
        run: cargo update -p openintents --manifest-path sdk/rust/Cargo.toml
      - id: commit
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit -am "chore(release): v$VERSION"
          git tag "v$VERSION"
          git push origin HEAD:main "v$VERSION"
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  npm:
    name: npm
    needs: prepare
    if: ${{ inputs.typescript }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sha }}
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents test
      - run: pnpm --filter @tinyhumansai/openintents build
      - run: npm publish --access public --provenance
        working-directory: sdk/typescript
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

  pypi:
    name: PyPI
    needs: prepare
    if: ${{ inputs.python }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: Production
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sha }}
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
      - run: uv run --extra dev pytest
        working-directory: sdk/python
      - run: uv build
        working-directory: sdk/python
      - run: uv publish dist/*
        working-directory: sdk/python
        env:
          UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}

  crates:
    name: crates.io
    needs: prepare
    if: ${{ inputs.rust }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sha }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - run: cargo test --locked
        working-directory: sdk/rust
      - run: cargo publish --locked
        working-directory: sdk/rust
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
